answer.evidence: This is a loose scatter of flat grey fragments, about 12 rows tall and not a single standing volume. The upper slab (rows 20-22) is a light band with a dark edge line at row 23 and a shadow at row 24. It has almost no front face below that, only 1-2 rows. The lower-left chunk (rows 26-29) is light on top with a dark base at rows 30-31. The lower-right fragment is 1 light row (27) over a dark edge (28) and 2 mid-tone rows (29-30). The fragments are separated by transparent gaps (for example x=16, rows 25-26). Some pieces show a top and a thin face, but there is no consistent 3+ row front face, so it fits neither three_quarter nor a pure slab. It reads as flat floor debris.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny, low, sparse grey scatter of rubble, much smaller than the references (hedge, stall, well). It shows about 3 grey tones with little clustering. The stones are not shaded one by one, and there are no per-stone highlights or grain. Dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line rather than a tinted material tone. This is the sticker look, unlike the hedge, stall and well, which have tinted edges (0-33% neutral). The tile-density fact is 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. Next to the references it looks thinner, flatter and less shaded than a Beodeul stone element such as the well's stonework. A careful artist would not accept it beside them.
